title: Reform UK's Racist Councillor Wins in Sunderland Landslide
excerpt: Glenn Gibbins secured a council seat in Hylton Castle despite deleted Facebook posts containing overtly racist remarks about Nigerians.
body:
Glenn Gibbins, a Reform UK candidate for Hylton Castle Ward in Sunderland, won a seat on Sunderland City Council on May 8, 2026 — despite a trail of deleted social media posts containing racist and misogynistic remarks that surfaced before polling day.

**What happened:**
Anti-racism group Hope Not Hate unearthed posts in which Gibbins wrote that he 'carnt believe the amount of Nigerians in town' and that officials should 'melt them all down and fill in the pot holes.' He also called female TV presenters 'repulsive' and wrote that women commentators should 'stick to cooking and home making.' Reform UK did not withdraw his candidacy. Gibbins pulled 1,295 votes, comfortably winning one of three seats in the ward.

**Why it matters beyond Sunderland:**
Gibbins' victory is not an isolated anomaly — it sits inside a political earthquake. Reform UK swept Sunderland City Council in its entirety, winning 58 of 75 seats and ending Labour's 52-year grip on the authority. Nigel Farage's party also took control of councils in Gateshead, South Tyneside, Essex, and Havering on the same night, prompting Farage to declare 'a truly historic shift in British politics.' Critics argue the Gibbins episode exposes a systematic failure by Reform UK to vet its candidates, raising serious questions about who now holds local power over diverse communities across northern England.

**What to watch:**
Sunderland City Council is expected to hold its annual general meeting later in May to confirm leadership positions — and whether Reform UK moves to distance itself from Gibbins, or quietly absorbs the controversy, will signal how seriously the party takes accountability from within.
